title: Open a folder to start working
subtitle: Point Ontology Atlas at a Markdown folder on this Mac. The files remain the local source of truth and Atlas does not upload them; a coding agent you later connect may send prompts and context to its own provider.
openBody: Pick an existing markdown folder and enter the workspace.
justStartBody: Creates it under Ontology Atlas in your home folder: no picker. Your AI agent can read and write it too.
justStartToast: Created at {path}: your AI agent can see this folder too.
createBody: Pick an empty folder and the starter structure is scaffolded for you: 5 markdown seeds plus agent configs.
demoBody: Explore the map Ontology Atlas draws of itself before opening your own folder.
starterFailed: The folder opened, but its starter files could not be written. Add them from Settings › Workspace.
errorFallback: Could not open the folder. Try again.
errorRootRejected: This folder can't be used as a map. Pick a folder that holds your documents, not a system folder or your whole home folder.
trustLine: Local Markdown is the source of truth · no Atlas backend
errorPathMissing: That folder is gone. It looks like it was moved or deleted. Pick another one.
errorPermission: Atlas cannot read this folder. Pick it again to grant access.
errorPermissionDenied: macOS is protecting the folder “{folder}”. Allow Ontology Atlas in System Settings under Privacy & Security, then Files and Folders, and open it again.
shapeTitle: Pick what to start with. The folder gets the same tree either way, and you can add the other part later from Settings.
shapeWikiBody: Your files go in sources/, and an agent writes one wiki page per document. No map, no code needed.
shapeMapTitle: An ontology map of a codebase
shapeMapBody: Starter nodes and agent skills for describing what the code builds and why. No wiki.
shapeBothBody: The map and the wiki side by side, with the wiki able to propose nodes to the map.
